commit_subject: Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing
description: independent review fixed two actionable findings: incomplete current child-deduction bands and an incorrectly anchored wagering proof

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The child-deduction table encoded the superseded pre-2022 schedule — six bands per filing status topping out at $2,500 — while the cited §105-153.5(a1) states seven bands per status topping out at $3,000 (MFJ bounds 40k/60k/80k/100k/120k/140k), so every child deduction came out $500 low and the top band was missing.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read and matched cell by cell against the pinned successor (corpus b403bf49, §105-153.5(a1)): 'Married, filing jointly/ Up to $40,000 $3,000 ... Over $120,000 Up to $140,000 500.00 Over $140,000 0', Head of Household to $105,000, Single and MFS to $70,000 — identical to the post-fix 28-entry tables. The same commit also fixes the version window from the timeless effective_from '0001-01-01' to '2022-01-01' and repoints the citation from the .../105-153.5/a1 fragment to the section, so this module carries a wrong_period_or_effective_date aspect as well; I tagged amount_mismatch because the decisive change is the replacement of every band bound and deduction amount. Pre-fix summary even self-described as 'Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022', yet the module fed the TY2026 resident pipeline.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module was not a botched transcription of the current table: its own summary declared it encoded the schedule "Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022", and its six-band / $2,500-max values are a faithful encoding of that superseded pre-2022 §105-153.5(a1) text — but all three parameter tables carried `effective_from: '0001-01-01'` with no `effective_to`, so superseded text applied for all time, including the TY2026 pipeline that consumed it. The fix narrows the window to `effective_from: '2022-01-01'`, repoints `corpus_citation_path` from the stale `/a1` predecessor fragment to `us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5`, and swaps in the current seven-band / $3,000 schedule; the commit subject ("Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing") and PR bullets ("repoint … from stale predecessor fragments to the official TY2026 temporal statute successor"; "This is a legitimate temporal/source-structure repair") frame it the same way. The kind taxonomy assigns exactly this pattern — "timeless encoding of superseded text" — to wrong_period_or_effective_date, so the changed cell values are the symptom of a version-anchoring defect rather than an independent amount error. It is still a fidelity defect (the numbers really were wrong for TY2026), so only the kind changes, not the classification.
triage.verifier_quote:
-    Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022, a taxpayer allowed a federal child tax credit under section 24 is allowed a North Carolina deduction for each qualifying child, with the per-child amount set by filing status and federal adjusted gross income.
-      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
+      - effective_from: '2022-01-01'
triage.verifier_notes:
Verified source text: the resolver (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfbda, provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-nc/statute/2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl line 52, body sha256 f40ff33b90…) gives current §105-153.5(a1) as seven bands per filing status topping at $3,000 with MFJ bounds 40k/60k/80k/100k/120k/140k, HoH 30/45/60/75/90/105k, Single and MFS 20/30/40/50/60/70k. The post-fix tables match that exactly; the pre-fix tables match the pre-2022 statute exactly (same bounds minus the top band, every amount $500 lower, $2,500 max). So the pre-fix numbers were internally coherent law, just the wrong vintage — that is the reason I moved the kind.

Two honest counterweights for the reviewer, which is why confidence is 0.6 and not higher: (1) resolving the pre-fix citation path `us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/a1` at the parent commit 5c087fc884 through the same pinned corpus returns the CURRENT text ($3,000, seven bands, sha256 2422c4d27b…) — the stale predecessor fragment is no longer reachable, so a reviewer who defines "the cited source" as what that path resolves to today would legitimately keep amount_mismatch, since the encoded cells disagree with the resolvable cited text. (2) The diff really does change ~60 table cells and add a band per status, and the PR bullet "encode the current §105-153.5 child-deduction bands" supports the numeric framing. If the corpus rubric prefers root cause, this is wrong_period_or_effective_date; if it prefers the surface of what the fix edited, amount_mismatch survives.

Separately, the first reader's justification quote ("independent review fixed two actionable findings: incomplete current child-deduction bands and an incorrectly anchored wagering proof") is weak evidence for the pre-fix defect: it describes findings raised and fixed inside PR #1106's own review cycle against an intermediate head, not the state of main before d1ed1b5949, and the "wagering proof" half belongs to a different module (the §165(d) itemized component, not a1.yaml). The decisive evidence for this module is the diff itself plus the old summary line.

Not mechanical: parameter values and version windows both changed. Not not_a_defect: the module fed us-nc/policies/income_tax/resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml for TY2026, so the superseded schedule was live, producing child deductions $500 low per band with the >120k band wrongly zeroed at what the current law makes a $500 band.
